questions.stem: Environment Canada has issued a gale warning for your area. What wind speed does that mean?
questions.explanation: A gale warning is for 34 to 47 knots. 20 to 33 is a strong wind warning and 48 to 63 is a storm warning.

questions.stem: What is the lowest of the Canadian marine wind warnings, and its range?
questions.explanation: The strong wind warning, 20 to 33 knots, is the lowest wind warning and is dangerous for small boats.

questions.stem: Who should hold your trip plan (sail plan)?
questions.explanation: Leave it with someone you trust who will act if you do not come back on time.

questions.stem: You are three hours overdue. What should the person holding your trip plan do?
questions.explanation: If you are overdue, your contact calls a JRCC to start a search.

questions.stem: You get home safely but forget to call the person holding your trip plan. What can happen?
options: A search may start for nothing
questions.explanation: Always close your trip plan. Otherwise a needless search may tie up rescuers.

questions.stem: Using the one-third rule, how should your fuel be split?
options: A third out, back and reserve
Two thirds out, a third back
A quarter each way, half spare
questions.explanation: Use one third to go out, one third to come back, and keep one third in reserve.

questions.stem: Your trip out will use 20 litres and the trip back 20 litres. Under the one-third rule, what is the least fuel you should leave with?
questions.explanation: Out and back are two thirds of the total, so each third is 20 litres. 3 x 20 = 60 litres.

questions.stem: Where should you fill a portable gas tank for your outboard?
options: In the cabin, out of wind
questions.explanation: Remove portable tanks from the boat and fill them ashore or on the dock.

questions.stem: After fuelling a boat with an inboard gasoline engine, how long should the blower run before you start the engine?
questions.explanation: Run the blower for at least 4 minutes, then sniff the engine space for fuel fumes before starting.

questions.stem: You smell gasoline in the engine space after running the blower. What should you do?
options: Do not start; find the leak
questions.explanation: A fuel smell means vapour is still there. Do not start the engine until the leak is found and fixed.

questions.stem: Which of these is an early sign of carbon monoxide poisoning?
questions.explanation: Headache, nausea, dizziness and itchy eyes are early signs, often mistaken for seasickness.

questions.stem: Why is teak surfing behind a boat so dangerous?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide builds up near the swim platform and back deck while engines run. Never sit, hang on or teak surf there.

questions.stem: You plan to cross a BC pass where a strong ebb current runs west. The forecast is a strong west wind blowing toward the east. What should you expect at peak ebb?
questions.explanation: Wind blowing against the current builds short, steep, breaking seas. Cross when wind and current go the same way, or near slack.

questions.stem: You are out on the water and want the latest marine forecast. Where can you get it?
questions.explanation: Marine forecasts are broadcast on VHF radio and posted online. Keep checking them while you are out.
